chapter: Discovering Henderson, clarinet and first gigs
title: Hearing Fletcher Henderson's band at 14 or 15 and deciding on music
summary: At a dance at the Renaissance Casino he hears Henderson, with Louis Armstrong in the band, and stands in front of the bandstand all night; he decides then what to do with his life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Now, you -- now, what is this about Lieutenant Eugene Mikell and the 369th [Street] Cadets?
Oh, I was growing up then. I wasn't growing up, but that was after I -- I was about --
Would you like to take that and put it behind you?

Yeah, yeah. That's a good idea, yeah. I was about -- put it like this. Yeah. Yeah. Nice. Thanks. At that time, you see, I had -- I never could remember whether this was before -- well, when I was about 14 or 15 years old I discovered Fletcher Henderson's band, because I went to a dance. Fletcher Henderson was playing at the Roseland Ballroom, Roseland Ballroom in New York, and so all these clubs, you know, these colored clubs, used to give these big dances and they used to give dances at the Renaissance Casino. The Savoy wasn't built yet. The Renaissance Casino, the Star Casino, wherever, uptown, so Fletcher used to get -- they used to hire Fletcher as an attraction and he'd come uptown and play an hour after his Roseland date. Then they'd advertise Fletcher Henderson, and there were big crowds, you know. And the house band was John C. Smith. You know he had a sedate band. They just played

stock arrangements, you know, till Fletcher got there, then he'd turn on the jazz. So anyhow, so you know, young kids, we went to this dance. It cost $1.10 to go to the dance. So we saved our money and we went to the dance.
That was a lot of money then, wasn't it?

Oh, yeah, $1.10. It took you all day -- it took you all month to get $1.10. My mother used to give us a dollar to go to the store and come back with a bag of groceries this high for $1.10, $1.25, you know. Well, anyhow, I -- well, we, I'd say -- we were there, because Louis Armstrong was getting real famous. Everybody was talking about him. In those days we called him Fats Armstrong. Fats Armstrong. You know, Coleman Hawkins, and we'd heard the records. So anyway, I went to this dance and I heard Fletcher Henderson's band, and I just stood there with my mouth open all night. I didn't move away from the front of the bandstand. Oh, I never heard anything like that in my life. And I think right then I decided what I was going to do with my life. Right then. You couldn't tell me anything about school, you couldn't tell me anything about work, or anything. That was it. From then on I just dreamed, you know, music, and --
Was this when Louis was with the band?
This was when he was with it?
Yeah. Yeah, Louis was with the band. This was in 19 --

I think it was before that. No, it was before '25. Louis was with --well, anyway, Louis was with it. I just read Max Jones' book about Louis Armstrong a couple of weeks ago. Louis was only with Fletcher about a year, was it?
Yeah, well, anyway, he was with it. What year was it, '24?
